steps.prompt: Before the check: write a topic sentence and one piece of evidence about any topic you like.

cards.title: Body paragraphs: quick review
cards.body: Topic sentence that links to the thesis → evidence (fact or number, example, quote with its source) → explanation (“This shows that…”) → link back. Informative: explain, don’t argue. Narrative: events in order with time words. Counterclaim (“Some people argue…”) → rebuttal (“However, …”) with evidence.

cards.title: Two body paragraphs
cards.body: In the writing task, paragraph 1 proves one reason from the thesis; paragraph 2 gives the other side and answers it. Leave a blank line between them. The essay map marks each topic sentence, its evidence, the counterclaim and the rebuttal.

cards.title: How the check works
cards.body: First, a 10-question quiz: you need 8 right (80%) to pass. If you don’t pass, you’ll see which skills to review, and you’ll get new questions next time. Then you’ll write two body paragraphs: one reason and one counterclaim paragraph. Quill gives them a score.

prompts: Which part of a body paragraph is now easiest for you? Which is still hard?
How will you choose evidence next time?
